200.title: Polish WWII massacre victims reburied in Ukraine at ceremony attended by officials from both countries
200.summary: Polish WWII massacre victims reburied in Ukraine at ceremony attended by officials from both countries Aug 31, 2026 | History , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
200.body: Polish WWII massacre victims reburied in Ukraine at ceremony attended by officials from both countries Aug 31, 2026 | History , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The remains of 55 Poles – around half of them children – massacred by Ukrainian nationalists in World War Two have been reburied at a ceremony in Ukraine attended by political and religious figures from both countries. “This is an important moment for [the victims’] families, but also the Polish state, because this funeral follows decades of waiting,” said Polish culture minister Marta Cienkowska at the ceremony in Ostrówki (Ostrovky in Ukrainian), a depopulated former village that, before the war, was part of Poland and now lies in Ukraine. The remains of a further 55 victims of massacres by Ukrainian nationalists during WWII have been exhumed in Ukraine.

WB Electronics, whose factory caught fire shortly in the early hours of Monday, is one of Poland’s largest private defense companies. 400.title: Scotland ranks third in Europe for foreign investment in energy, report finds
400.summary: SCOTLAND attracted more energy-related Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) projects in 2025 than every other country in Europe except France and Germany, according to a new report from service giant EY.
400.body: SCOTLAND attracted more energy-related Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) projects in 2025 than every other country in Europe except France and Germany, according to a new report from service giant EY. The company – one of the “Big Four” professional services firms – said that Scotland had seen 15 FDI energy projects in 2025, 55% of the UK’s total of 27. Europe as a whole attracted 177 energy FDI projects in 2025, a 36% year-on-year decrease following the 275 projects secured in 2024. Scottish Energy Minister Stephen Gethins welcomed the report, saying it demonstrates “that Scotland’s energy sector is one of the true leaders of the energy transition with the ability to attract serious and sustained inward investment in the face of global economic uncertainties”.
